Thought: To find the mass of one gold atom, I need to use Avogadro's constant, which tells me how many atoms are in one mole of a substance. Since gold has a relative mass of 197, this means that one mole of gold has a mass of 197 g. If I divide this mass by Avogadro's constant, I'll get the mass of one gold atom.

Mass of one gold atom = Mass of one mole of gold / Avogadro's constant
Mass of one gold atom = 197 g / 6.02E23 mol^-1

Let me calculate this:
Mass of one gold atom = 197 g / (6.02 × 10^23) mol^-1
Mass of one gold atom = 197 g / (6.02 × 10^23)
Mass of one gold atom = 3.27243 × 10^-22 g

Note: The density information (19.3 g cm^-3) wasn't needed for this calculation.
